judgments.reasoning_cat1: The instruction that "Student and parent must determine the age of legal competency to sign contracts" pushes a legal question onto the signers without saying what follows if the determination is wrong, and "in most states" makes the minority threshold indefinite. judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with c016, which says the description is "not complete" and extends to unknown risks, and with c017's release, the enumerated-risk recital and the sweeping operative assumption pull in somewhat different directions. judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line descriptive statement that NOLS activities "may be strenuous, physically and emotionally"; nothing operative and nothing to construe. "Strenuous" is general but no obligation turns on it.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c016's assumption of inherent risks and with c019's allocation of evacuation costs to the student; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Equipment may fail or malfunction" is short but unambiguous as a risk disclosure; it names no obligation and no term whose meaning could be contested. Its brevity does not create a construction question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Descriptive camping and food risks; "Camping risks include" is an open list but nothing operative depends on where the list stops. "Offending food types" is loose but harmless.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long enumeration closed by "other means" and "other risks usually associated with such travel," a classic general-following-specifics construction, and the text is interrupted by page-footer garbage. Still, it is disclosure, not obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Vehicle travel overlaps with the private-contractor disclaimer in c014, but the two can be harmonised; no contradiction identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The catch-alls "forces of nature" and "other mild or serious conditions" are open-ended, but they close a purely illustrative risk list. Nothing in it fixes a party's rights.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Characterising staff decisions as "imprecise and subject to errors in judgment" blurs the line between an inherent risk and ordinary negligence, and "misjudgments" is exactly the term a plaintiff and defendant would read differently. It is the one risk bullet that speaks to human fault.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read against c017, which releases negligence but expressly not gross negligence or intentional wrongdoing, and against c016's assumption of "ALL risks"; whether an instructor's misjudgment is an assumed inherent risk or excluded gross negligence is a genuine internal question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain factual disclosure that students sometimes travel without instructors; "most NOLS courses" and "at times" are hedges, not ambiguities affecting any obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with c011's statement that NOLS cannot continually monitor students; no provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Free" is placed in scare quotes and the clause disclaims responsibility "before and after" the course while conceding free time also occurs "during" it, leaving in-course free time unallocated; "acting as private individuals" is a further contestable characterisation. Those are namable ambiguities on which liability could turn.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The release in c017 covers claims "arising in whole or part from... enrollment or participation in an activity of NOLS," and it is unclear how that meshes with time NOLS says it has no responsibility for at all, or with the staff-as-private-individuals carve-out against the defined "Released Parties." judgments.reasoning_cat1: The last sentence — foreign field practices are "generally consistent with customs and standards used in the United States" — reads as an affirmative assurance with an undefined qualifier ("generally"), and is the sort of sentence a plaintiff would call a representation. The preceding risk list is unproblematic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That assurance sits awkwardly beside c016's assumption of ALL risks and c018's statement that admission is no representation about NOLS' capabilities; a standard-of-care representation inside a risk disclosure is in some tension with the wholesale disclaimers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence describing the instructional character of the program; nothing operative and no contestable term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c009 (student and staff judgment) and c016; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "NOLS is not responsible for the acts or omissions of such contractors" is an operative exculpation buried in an illustrative risk list, and "private contractors" is undefined and illustrated only by "transportation." Whether a given provider is a contractor or an agent is exactly the argument the wording invites.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The "Released Parties" defined in c017 include "agents" and staff but not contractors, while c009 lumps "contractors" in with instructors and staff; the instrument therefore treats contractors inconsistently across provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It acknowledges reading a set of named external documents plus "other material provided by NOLS describing or related to my program," an open catch-all after specifics, and says staff "has been available" rather than that anything was actually explained. The reach of the incorporated material is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Whether the Catalog, website and Enrollment Packet become terms matters against c024's "MAY BE MODIFIED ONLY IN WRITING" and the assumption of risk in c016, since outside materials could describe risks or standards differently. That is a plausible but unproven fit problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-out "except with respect to an injury or other loss which occurs on lands whose rules or regulations prohibit my doing so as a matter of law" is opaque — which lands, whose rules, and what makes a prohibition operate "as a matter of law" are all left open — while "ALL risks... inherent or otherwise" is deliberately sweeping. This is a one-sided drafter's clause with a namable ambiguous exception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with c002's inherent-risk definition, with c017's parallel but separately worded carve-out, and with c009/c014's negligence-adjacent disclaimers; assuming "ALL risks" including negligence sits uneasily with c017's express exclusion of gross negligence. A court construing the release would necessarily construe this alongside it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This is the operative exculpatory and indemnity clause: it releases "any and all claims... arising in whole or part from" participation, includes negligence "but not of gross negligence," is to be "enforced to the fullest extent permitted by law," and carries the same murky lands-rules carve-out. Each of those phrases is a standard battleground, and the clause is drafted wholly in the drafter's favour, so any ambiguity is construed against NOLS.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its defined "Released Parties" omit the contractors disclaimed in c014 and the staff who under c011 act "as private individuals" during free time, and its scope must be squared with c016's assumption of ALL risks and c023's severability. Those interactions give a court more than one place to find inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "No past or current physical or psychological condition that might affect... participation" and "all pertinent medical conditions have been disclosed" set an indefinite standard, and NOLS may remove a student "for any reason it deems in the best interests" — discretion with no measurable boundary. A misrepresentation fight would turn on "might affect" and "pertinent."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The disclaimer that admission is not a representation that staff can manage a medical event sits alongside c019's authorisation for NOLS to provide advanced care under written Medical Protocols, which is close to an assumed standard; the two are in mild tension. No outright contradiction was found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Costs reasonably associated with medical services, including evacuation, shall be borne by me" hinges on the undefined qualifier "reasonably," and the reference to care "under the guidance of the NOLS Physician Advisor by way of NOLS' written Medical Protocols" imports an unattached external document. Both are namable but modest.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Environmental organizations or strategic partners in which NOLS graduates may be interested" is vague at the edges, but the grant of permission itself is clear and unconditional. Little turns on where "strategic partners" stops.
